title: Maximum Enemy Forts That Can Be Captured
summary: Given an array forts of length n where each element is -1, 0, or 1 representing the presence or absence of forts, calculate the maximum number of enemy forts (0) that can be captured by moving your army from one of your forts (1) over only enemy forts.
statement: Given an array forts of length n where each element is -1, 0, or 1 representing the presence or absence of forts, calculate the maximum number of enemy forts (0) that can be captured by moving your army from one of your forts (1) over only enemy forts. Return 0 if no such move is possible or if you have no forts under your command.
constraints: Values are 1 for your fort, -1 for an enemy fort, and 0 for empty positions.
You may capture empty positions strictly between two nearest nonzero forts of opposite signs.
Return the maximum number of captured empty positions, or zero if no such interval exists.
hints: Only consecutive nonzero forts can bound a valid all-zero interval.
Remember the index of the previous nonzero fort while scanning.
When the current sign is opposite, maximize current_index-previous_index-1.
Any interval with another fort inside is invalid, so checking consecutive nonzero endpoints covers every possible capture.
editorial: Any interval with another fort inside is invalid, so checking consecutive nonzero endpoints covers every possible capture.

tests.explanation: The four zeros between the enemy fort and the final friendly fort form the largest capturable interval.
Opposite forts are adjacent, so zero empty positions are captured.
